4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: With its massive budget and Kcirbuk's directorial cachet, this drama was set to be a milestone for Sordland's burgeoning film scene. Personally, though, I was just looking forward to spending some time with my family.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: It was a very hot and sunny day as Serge drove us to the old capital. The film was to be screened in the historic Cinema Anglei dei Erlory -- the very first cinema in Sordland.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: Serge had maxed out the air conditioning to keep the Kadilla comfortable. I kept silent through most of our ride on the H-1. I couldn't get my mind off the results of the Assembly vote.
6.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_P_SupportedMonicaAtConfrontation"] == true)

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: I gazed at the vast plains between Holsord and Erlory as we drove on the H-1. Serge had maxed out the air conditioning to keep the Kadilla comfortable.
13.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_P_SupportedMonicaAtConfrontation"] == true)

17.speaker: Monica
17.text: "If you were going to bring your work stress into this, you shouldn't have taken us along."

21.speaker: Monica
21.text: "If you were going to bring your work stress into this, you shouldn't have taken us along."

22.speaker: Monica
22.text: "All she wanted to do was cheer you up."

24.speaker: Player
24.text: "I know, I know. I didn't mean to make her sad..."

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: Besides which, Petr had worked hard with the producers to make this screening possible during the emergency, albeit with limited attendance and heavy security.

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: Serge rolled down the soundproof glass between us.

33.speaker: Monica
33.text: "How very presidential of you, making decisions on behalf of the rest of us."

37.speaker: Monica
37.text: "Just watch your tone with the kids, Anton. Please control your stress."

39.speaker: Monica
39.text: "It's okay. But please watch your tone with the kids, Anton."

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: Franc turned toward us for the first time since he'd gotten in the car.

41.speaker: Serge Wolkner
41.text: "Sir, we are about to enter Erlory. We'll be at the cinema in a few minutes."

46.speaker: Franc
46.text: "My dad's just sick of us, Serge."

47.speaker: Narrator
47.text: I took a brief look outside as Serge rolled the soundproof glass up again.

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: I could see the many towers of Erlory rising over what was left of the old city walls.

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: I could see the many towers of Erlory rising over what was left of the old city walls.

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: In the distance, there were several planes flying towards the city.

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: As they got closer to us, I saw that they were military planes that looked like the sharp-edged Arcasian designs. They were probably headed for our new joint military base.

55.speaker: Serge Wolkner
55.text: "Hah, young sir, don't say that. Why would Mr. President get sick of you? He loves you all more than anything."

57.speaker: Player
57.text: "Franc, enough. Could you roll the glass up again, Serge?"

60.speaker: Serge Wolkner
60.text: "Oh, sir, I don't mind the young mister. He's an intelligent young man."

64.speaker: Serge Wolkner
64.text: "At any rate, we'll be there in a minute. I'll leave you to it for now."

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: Monica pointed at the hills on the outskirts of the city.

70.speaker: Player
70.text: "It's just behind those hills. We should go there sometime."

71.speaker: Player
71.text: "Yes. It's already started producing wine again, too. We'll have our own wine soon!"

72.speaker: Franc
72.text: "Rayne Wines! Made by a family who knows nothing about making wine!"

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "We're not the ones making the wine, genius."

85.speaker: Franc
85.text: "I know. Why lie? The truth always sounds better anyway."

87.speaker: Player
87.text: "Are you sure about that, son? Truth doesn't really sell."

89.speaker: Franc
89.text: "Yeah, okay. I know that my grandfather used to be a wine connoisseur or something. But did you really learn how to make wine?"

90.speaker: Franc
90.text: "I'm sorry. I guess you know everything, dad."

91.speaker: Player
91.text: "If only everyone thought like that, son..."

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: Serge knocked on the glass and gestured forwards.

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: We were at the main square of Erlory, and the historic 'Cinema Anglei'—the Cinema of Angels—was right in front of us.

100.speaker: Narrator
100.text: Franc fidgeted with his tie as he stared out the window.

101.speaker: Monica
101.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Bludish_Opinion"] <= 0  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_JointOperation"] == true) == false)

102.speaker: Narrator
102.text: It was an old baroque-style corner building with walls that looked like marble from a distance. There were exquisite ornaments on each side of every window.

103.speaker: Narrator
103.text: Serge pulled the car to the entrance of the building, which was lit by vivid neon stripes in many colors.

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: Serge opened the doors, and we exited onto the red carpet.

105.speaker: Narrator
105.text: In contrast with the cinema's baroque-style exterior, the inside was modern and sleek, with bare walls painted in black, red and white.

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: The film's cast and crew were already in the foyer, with glasses of champagne in their hands.

110.speaker: Narrator
110.text: Serge opened the doors, and we exited onto the red carpet.

114.speaker: Narrator
114.text: As they noticed us and our many guards, the mood in the room immediately soured.

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: We approached the crowd and were welcomed by the producers and the event organizers.

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: On the wall next to the entrance, there were painted the words "Stop The Oppression of Bluds".

123.speaker: Narrator
123.text: On the wall next to the entrance, there were painted the words "Stop The Oppression of Bluds".

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: Other graffiti next to it read, "Stop the Genocide in Wehlen" and "Axis of Evil: Smolak, Rayne, Lancea."

128.speaker: Narrator
128.text: As the police escorted us inside the cinema, a journalist broke through our security cordon and started running at me.

129.speaker: Narrator
129.text: As soon as he yelled "Mr. President!" one of the policemen kicked him in the back and forced him down onto the ground. Another grabbed me by the suit jacket and quickly ushered me away.

130.speaker: Narrator
130.text: He motioned for me and my family to continue along the security corridor.

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: A man walked up to us with quick steps.

137.speaker: Policeman
137.text: "We had to for your safety, sir."

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: He and the other guards seemed not to care what had just happened. We kept walking through the corridor.

139.speaker: Narrator
139.text: We were just about to enter the building when a journalist managed to block the path.

141.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
141.text: "Madame! Mr. President! It's so good to see you here."

142.speaker: Monica
142.text: "Why don't we take our seats? It's about to start."

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: He gently bowed at Monica and shook our hands.

144.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
144.text: "It's an honor to meet you. I'm Alfred Kcirbuk."

146.speaker: Player
146.text: "The honor is mine, Mr. Kcirbuk. I'm a big fan of your work."

147.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
147.text: "It's very humbling to know that you've been watching and enjoying my movies."

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: Franc snorted. I glanced at him, and he innocently took a sip of his cola.

149.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
149.text: "If you don't mind my asking, which one was your favorite? This one may be slightly different than my previous works."

151.speaker: Player
151.text: "All of them are my favourites, Mr. Kcirbuk."

152.speaker: Player
152.text: "I loved The Man Who Saved The World."

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: He stared at me for a while as if he was trying to understand if I was joking or not.

154.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
154.text: "You flatter me too much, Mr. President. I myself know they aren't all winners."

157.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
157.text: "That's by Mikel Vargas, Mr. President. It beat my film The Sordish Dream for the top prize at the Benfi Festival last year."

158.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
158.text: "Oh, really? Then you might enjoy this one too."

159.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
159.text: "I'll admit, I didn't expect you to be such a cinephile."

160.speaker: Narrator
160.text: Franc looked me in the eye and struggled not to laugh.

161.speaker: Narrator
161.text: Although I wasn't in much of a moviegoing mood, it would have been unpresidential not to attend.

167.speaker: Player_Italic
167.text: Ignore him and talk to Deana.

168.speaker: Franc
168.text: "Since when do you care what's happening in my life?"

169.speaker: Narrator
169.text: Serge had maxed out the air conditioning to keep the Kadilla comfortable. But that wasn't the only reason I felt a chill in the air.

171.speaker: Player
171.text: "I've been busy lately, but I'll always have time for you."

172.speaker: Player
172.text: "You know I'll support you whether you pass or fail those exams."

173.speaker: Narrator
173.text: I noticed Franc fidgeting with his tie anxiously.

176.speaker: Franc
176.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false)

180.speaker: Monica
180.text: "Franc, don't talk to your father that way! He tried his best."

187.speaker: Franc
187.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true)

192.speaker: Monica
192.text: "Franc, don't talk to your father that way! He's been working so hard for this country."

193.speaker: Player
193.text: "Are you having a good time, sweetie?"

194.speaker: Player
194.text: "Are you in a better mood than your brother?"

198.speaker: Narrator
198.text: Deana nodded shyly and hugged her stuffed animal closer to her chest. Monica draped a protective arm around her. Nobody spoke for the rest of the ride.

206.speaker: Player
206.text: "Hah! I won't lose. Isn't that right, Monica?"

207.speaker: Deana
207.text: "What about you, Papa? You won something, right? You should smile! And keep doing your best even if you lose."
207.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true)

208.speaker: Player
208.text: "I'm just fine, Deana. Everything's going to be wonderful from now on, right, Monica?"

210.speaker: Deana
210.text: "Don't worry about me, Papa! You've got the whole country to worry about!"

211.speaker: Deana
211.text: "What about you, Papa? I know you're sad, but failure helps us grow, right?"
211.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reformist_Path"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false)

212.speaker: Player
212.text: "Exactly! Now, where did you learn that?"

213.speaker: Player
213.text: "All I'm worried about is whether or not there will be popcorn."

222.speaker: Monica
222.text: "How should I know? I don't meddle in these affairs."

226.speaker: Player
226.text: "Everything's going to be wonderful from now on, isn't it, Monica?"

227.speaker: Player
227.text: "Now, no more politics talk! Isn't that right, Monica?"

229.speaker: Monica
229.text: "Of course. Let's just focus on having a nice time at the movies."

237.speaker: Monica
237.text: "I just want to focus on having a nice time at the movies."

238.speaker: Player
238.text: "Don't take that tone with me! You don't know the stress I'm under."

240.speaker: Monica
240.text: "Anton you can't act like this with us. I'm not your assistant."

241.speaker: Player
241.text: "Darling, we've been through this. I'm sorry."

242.speaker: Narrator
242.text: Monica folded her arms. We drove on in silence.

245.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
245.text: "The... the director of tonight's film. I was told you were a big fan of my work."

246.speaker: Alfred Kcirbuk
246.text: "My producers told me you had expressed admiration for my work."

247.speaker: Narrator
247.text: We entered the screening room, the lights dimmed, and the film began.

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: It was a period drama set in the 1870s, about a Sordish soldier who pursues a doomed romance with a widowed Bludish farmer during the conquest of Bergia.

249.speaker: Narrator
249.text: I wondered briefly whether Kcirbuk was commenting on my own treatment of the Bludish people. But then, he had finished filming long before I became president.

253.speaker: Narrator
253.text: As the credits rolled, I made an early exit to use the men's room. I was washing my hands when I heard an unmistakeable voice behind me.

255.speaker: Narrator
255.text: Tarquin Soll leaned on his cane. He had aged noticeably since the last time I saw him, his appearance far more frail. Yet beneath it all, I could still sense the raw magnetism that had kept him in power for 20 years.

259.speaker: Narrator
259.text: Tarquin Soll leaned on his cane. He had the same frail appearance I'd noticed at the Assembly meeting. Yet up close, I could still sense the raw magnetism that had kept him in power for 20 years.

260.speaker: Player
260.text: "Complete and utter drivel. What about yourself?"

264.speaker: Player
264.text: "Dangerous pro-Bludish propaganda. I ought to have it banned."

265.speaker: Player
265.text: "I'm happy the plight of the Bludish might finally get the attention it deserves."

266.speaker: Player
266.text: "I found the plot questionable, but it certainly looked spectacular. What about yourself?"

267.speaker: Tarquin Soll
267.text: "Sentimental pablum for the enjoyment of housewives only. And for a period piece, the script contained far too many anachronisms."

271.speaker: Tarquin Soll
271.text: "Be careful where you extend your sympathies, President Rayne."

272.speaker: Player
272.text: "What the hell are you doing here, Mr. Soll?"

273.speaker: Player
273.text: "What the hell were you doing at the Assembly vote, Mr. Soll?"

274.speaker: Player
274.text: "Enough small talk. What brought you here from your island?"

275.speaker: Player
275.text: "Enough small talk. Why were you at the Assembly vote?"

279.speaker: Tarquin Soll
279.text: "A man's got to get off his island every once in a while, you know."

280.speaker: Narrator
280.text: He smiled, but I could see no mirth on his face.

281.speaker: Tarquin Soll
281.text: "And I wanted to check in on how my country has been faring in my absence."

282.speaker: Tarquin Soll
282.text: "My country was about to make a rash decision. I couldn't simply sit by."

288.speaker: Player
288.text: "You've succeeded, for now. But you won't be able to stop me for long."

294.speaker: Narrator
294.text: There was a glint in his eye.

298.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
298.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Abolished"] == true   or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_NoImmunity"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false

300.speaker: Player
300.text: "I can handle Sordland without you, old man."

301.speaker: Player
301.text: "Your presence is appreciated. But I've got everything under control."

302.speaker: Narrator
302.text: There was a glint in his eye.

307.speaker: Tarquin Soll
307.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_AutocratEmergency_Extend"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_YS"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == false) == false)

308.speaker: Tarquin Soll
308.text: "I wouldn't be so sure about that."

309.speaker: Player
309.text: "You may still have your loyalists. But I'm the one in control."

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "I'm happy you're looking out for me. But I don't need any help."

311.speaker: Tarquin Soll
311.text: "I was wrong to champion you all those years ago. You proved to be a spineless weasel!"

315.speaker: Tarquin Soll
315.text: "Now, if you'll excuse me, I've got my garden to get back to. Someone has to keep the weeds from spreading."

316.speaker: Player
316.text: "And are you pleased with the outcome?"
316.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Abolished"] == true   or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_NoImmunity"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false

317.speaker: Narrator
317.text: Soll fixed me with a piercing stare. His back straightened.

321.speaker: Tarquin Soll
321.text: "Perhaps my clout with the Assembly isn't what it used to be. But you may yet encounter difficulties pushing your reforms through the Supreme Court."

324.speaker: Player
324.text: "You won't get away with your meddling."

325.speaker: Player
325.text: "A true president knows when he must step down."

326.speaker: Player
326.text: "But why did you block my reforms?"

327.speaker: Player
327.text: "Why do you want these reforms blocked so badly?"

328.speaker: Player
328.text: "A true president knows when he must step down."

333.speaker: Tarquin Soll
333.text: "I will not have my party and my Constitution tarnished by a tyrant."
333.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true)

334.speaker: Tarquin Soll
334.text: "I will not let you and that bleeding-heart idiot Ricter tarnish my precious Constitution."

338.speaker: Tarquin Soll
338.text: "I will not let an upstart like you tarnish my party and my Constitution."
338.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Dictator_Path"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_PFJP_Convinced"] == true) == false) and (((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false)

339.speaker: Tarquin Soll
339.text: "A lesson you'd be wise to learn yourself."

340.speaker: Player
340.text: "Ricter's a better man than you ever were."

341.speaker: Player
341.text: "Your Constitution is ancient history. My reforms will bring Sordland into the future."

343.speaker: Narrator
343.text: Some of his spittle landed on my cheek.

344.speaker: Player
344.text: "You tarnished it enough for the both of us already."

345.speaker: Player
345.text: "I'm doing this for the good of the country."

347.speaker: Narrator
347.text: Some of his spittle landed on my cheek.

348.speaker: Tarquin Soll
348.text: "I saw right through Ricter in the '30s, and he hasn't changed a bit. That man will do and say anything to advance his own cause."

349.speaker: Narrator
349.text: Some of his spittle landed on my cheek.

352.speaker: Narrator
352.text: Some of his spittle landed on my cheek.

357.speaker: Tarquin Soll
357.text: "If Sordland remains in your hands, the only future I see is anarchy."

361.speaker: Player
361.text: "I know, but I need him on my side to undo your damage."

365.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
365.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_NoImmunity"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Abolished"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false

366.speaker: Tarquin Soll
366.text: "I'm fully aware of your intention to punish me for some crime you think I committed. As if you, Anton Rayne, are above it all. As if you're capable of remaining president without getting your hands dirty."

367.speaker: Tarquin Soll
367.text: "As if you, Anton Rayne, are above it all. As if you're capable of remaining president without getting your hands dirty."
367.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_NoImmunity"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Abolished"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false

370.speaker: Player
370.text: "I'm no saint. But I'm trying to act for the good of the country."

371.speaker: Player
371.text: "I always looked up to you. Just give me a chance to do my job."

372.speaker: Tarquin Soll
372.text: "You'll find out soon enough how your country repays you for your 'goodness'."

373.speaker: Narrator
373.text: He slipped past me and out the door.

374.speaker: Narrator
374.text: Soll's security staff and mine were now clustered outside the washroom, forming a buffer against the large crowd that had gathered.

375.speaker: Narrator
375.text: "That's Tarquin Soll!" I heard someone scream. His guards closed around him, and mine around me.

376.speaker: Narrator
376.text: By the time the chaos subsided, I was back in the car with my family, and Soll was long gone.

377.speaker: Narrator
377.text: I stormed past him and out the door.

381.speaker: Tarquin Soll
381.text: "I've known it since you opposed me all those years ago. You spineless backstabbing weasel!"
381.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_MinisterOffer_Accepted"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_MinisterOffer_Accepted"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_MinisterOffer_Rejected"] == false)

382.speaker: Tarquin Soll
382.text: "I've known it since you turned down the position I offered you all those years ago. You spineless weasel!"
382.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_MinisterOffer_Accepted"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_MinisterOffer_Accepted"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Prologue_MinisterOffer_Rejected"] == false) == false)

383.speaker: Tarquin Soll
383.text: "You took the court's advice and extended the state of emergency. Very prudent."

384.speaker: Player
384.text: "Thanks, Colonel. Your opinion means a lot."

385.speaker: Player
385.text: "Anything to keep my enemies at bay."

386.speaker: Player
386.text: "I'm surprised to see you here, sir."

387.speaker: Player
387.text: "I'm surprised to see you're still around, sir. What were you doing at the Assembly?"

390.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
390.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false

395.speaker: Tarquin Soll
395.text: "I'll tell you who I was wrong about: you. You spineless weasel!"

396.speaker: Tarquin Soll
396.text: "I'm right about him, the same way I was right never to trust you. You spineless weasel!"

397.speaker: Tarquin Soll
397.text: "You have no idea what it takes to do this job, boy. But you'll find out soon enough."

401.speaker: Player
401.text: "At last, I can admit it: I never did like you."

402.speaker: Player
402.text: "I still have immense respect for you, Colonel. I wish it was reciprocated."

403.speaker: Tarquin Soll
403.text: "It will be when you prove yourself worthy of it."

407.speaker: Player
407.text: "The Assembly considers me worthy. Doesn't that count for anything?"

408.speaker: Tarquin Soll
408.text: "If Sordland remains in your hands, the only future I see is misery."

409.speaker: Player
409.text: "There's nothing you can do anymore, old man."

410.speaker: Player
410.text: "Well-spoken as always. We'll see how well it serves you during your trial."

413.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
413.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Abolished"] == true   or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_NoImmunity"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false

414.speaker: Player
414.text: "You had your chance to lead. Everyone saw what a mess you made of it."
414.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Abolished"] == true   or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_NoImmunity"] == true)  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_AssemblyVote_Success"] == true) == false

417.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
417.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_YS"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == false) == false

418.speaker: Tarquin Soll
418.text: "I wouldn't be so sure about that."
418.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_AutocratEmergency_Extend"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_YS"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == false)

419.speaker: Player
419.text: "I can handle Sordland without you, old man."

420.speaker: Tarquin Soll
420.text: "Banning the Young Sords, while the communists and Bludish scum run rampant?"

421.speaker: Tarquin Soll
421.text: "Why did you end the state of emergency so prematurely?"

422.speaker: Player
422.text: "Do you see me as your puppet?"

424.speaker: Player
424.text: "You could have spoken to me about it directly."

425.speaker: Player
425.text: "The country still needs to be brought out of recession. This was a distraction."

426.speaker: Player
426.text: "I judged that the worst of the threat was over."

427.speaker: Player
427.text: "It was reflecting badly on my reputation as a democratic leader."

428.speaker: Player
428.text: "It was a hard decision, but I did what I had to."

429.speaker: Player
429.text: "I wanted to stop the violence. They were the worst offenders."

430.speaker: Player
430.text: "They had to be punished for Circas' murder."

438.speaker: Tarquin Soll
438.text: "Your decision not to ban the Workers Party of Bludia may cause problems, however. They clearly are a continuation of the Bludish Freedom Front."

439.speaker: Tarquin Soll
439.text: "Your decision not to ban the Red Youth may cause problems, however."

440.speaker: Player
440.text: "A ban will only lead to further violence."

442.speaker: Tarquin Soll
442.text: "Short-sighted. I tried to warn Hawker about you."

444.speaker: Tarquin Soll
444.text: "Do you truly believe Hawker came to you of his own accord?"

446.speaker: Player
446.text: "Wait. The emergency declaration was your idea?"

449.speaker: Tarquin Soll
449.text: "How do you think I've been spending my retirement? Just tending to my garden in my island?"

450.speaker: Tarquin Soll
450.text: "I've got to protect my party and my legacy somehow. Hawker and Graf advise me on how."

451.speaker: Tarquin Soll
451.text: "I told Hawker you could be counted on to make the right choice."

452.speaker: Player
452.text: "The police are doing enough to keep the Bludish in line."

453.speaker: Player
453.text: "The police are already doing enough to keep the communists in line."

454.speaker: Player
454.text: "The Bludish were your problem, not mine."

455.speaker: Player
455.text: "The communists were your problem, not mine."

457.speaker: Tarquin Soll
457.text: "Our problems are one and the same. Do you truly believe Hawker came to you of his own accord?"

458.speaker: Tarquin Soll
458.text: "And what good would that have done? You haven't trusted me since the Party Congress."

462.speaker: Player
462.text: "I've always looked up to you. Just give me a chance to do my job."

463.speaker: Tarquin Soll
463.text: "You have no idea what it takes to do this job, boy. But you'll find out soon enough."

464.speaker: Narrator
464.text: He slipped past me and out the door.

470.speaker: Tarquin Soll
470.text: "I see you as a novice in need of some valuable guidance."

472.speaker: Player
472.text: "You had your chance to lead. Everyone saw what a mess you made."

473.speaker: Player
473.text: "I'm warning you, sir. Stay out of my presidency."

474.speaker: Narrator
474.text: Soll fixed me with a piercing stare. He was an old man now -- how could he still be so intimidating?

476.speaker: Reporter
476.text: "Your constitutional reforms made it through the Assembly -- how do you feel about their chances with the Supreme Court?"

483.speaker: Reporter
483.text: "How are you handling the defeat of your constitutional reforms in the Assembly?"

484.speaker: Reporter
484.text: "Thank you, Mr. President. And were you aware that Tarquin Soll would be present at the proceedings?"

485.speaker: Reporter
485.text: "You recently rescinded your emergency declaration. Do you feel that the state has achieved its goals?"

486.speaker: Player
486.text: "Yes, the threats to the nation have been neutralized."

487.speaker: Player
487.text: "Our enemies are still out there. But we cannot keep living in fear."

488.speaker: Player
488.text: "Declaring the emergency was a mistake. The country's back on the right path now."

498.speaker: Reporter
498.text: "One more question. Can you comment on the arrests of Marcel Koronti and Walter Tusk following the state takeovers of their companies?"

499.speaker: Reporter
499.text: "One more question. Can you comment on the arrest of Marcel Koronti following the state takeover of his corporation?"

500.speaker: Reporter
500.text: "One more question. Can you comment on the arrest of Walter Tusk following the state takeover of his corporation?"

503.speaker: Player
503.text: "An unfortunate casualty, but nationalization is the only way forward."

513.speaker: Player
513.text: "I'm going to keep fighting for my changes. This isn't over yet."

517.speaker: Player
517.text: "No, I had to find out from my driver."

518.speaker: Player
518.text: "I refuse to discuss Colonel Soll at this time."

519.speaker: Player
519.text: "I trust the justices will make the right decision."

520.speaker: Player
520.text: "The court will vote my way if they know what's good for them."

521.speaker: Player
521.text: "One way or another, these reforms will pass."

525.speaker: Narrator
525.text: Before she could ask anything else, the guards ushered us inside the theater.

528.speaker: Narrator
528.text: Franc turned his head away to look outside the window.

529.speaker: Player
529.text: "*You* calling me a tyrant, of all people?"
